pairs.difference: A: the jacket has three separate masses: khaki-cream cloth, orange collar and cuffs, and a dark green sash. Its background green is echoed in the sash, so the hero's hues have clear roles. B: the hat is one terracotta-orange family across crown, brim and band. Its shadow side stays orange-brown with no cool or violet turn, like the lesson's generated gloves. The chroma numbers are nearly equal, so this rests on the eye only.
pairs.fix: Make the hat a dusty, slightly greyed tan felt. Let the underside of the brim fall into a cool plum-brown shadow, not orange. Keep the band a darker, separate brown.

pairs.difference: A: a saturated cobalt pillow on pale pink, with blue shadows that stay rich and related. Hero chroma is at the top of the real range, but the cards in image 1 carry similar single-hue heroes. B: the crimson field is near monochrome and the white print sits low on subject chroma, warm share and hue families. Those readings come from the large neutral white border, and the white itself stays clean and not creamy. Neither card shows a colour fault that the lessons tie to generated work.

A: the band slides from hot pink to orange with yellow-orange icons, so no neutral rests the eye on the hero. Subject chroma is just over the real ceiling and it competes with the loud cyan rings. B: the star keeps a neutral silver face, gold trim and a violet-leaning shadow under the centre disc, set on muted purple. The low hue count comes from gold and purple being a tight pair. The call is weak because the margins on both cards are small.
pairs.fix: Paint the wristband one slightly muted raspberry pink, with no slide into orange. Make the icons a soft pale gold. Calm the cyan background so the band is the only loud colour.

pairs.difference: A: orange posts, red ring and aqua water form distinct hue roles, though the deep-water shadows go dull teal and shadow chroma is below the real floor. B: tan walls, terracotta roof, red trim and sand sit in one warm family, with warm share above the real ceiling, and only the sky and windows break it. The cream-tan walls match the warmed neutrals on the generated computers. The violet shadow under the porch counts against this call, so confidence is low.
pairs.fix: Make the saloon walls a greyer, weathered wood instead of cream-tan. Let the shaded walls lean cool grey-violet, and mute the sand so the whole card is not pulled warm.

pairs.difference: A: the saddle and the rail are nearly one rust-orange mass on cyan, and the shadows just deepen to red-brown with no cool turn. This is the same orange-on-cyan push as the generated gloves. B: the beach ball has separate red, blue, green and lilac masses, and its pale panels stay lilac-grey up high. The red-orange shadow on the sand is strong, just above the real ceiling, and is the main doubt on this call.
pairs.fix: Make the saddle a deeper, browner leather and the rail a paler, greyer wood. Let shadows under the seat fall to cool plum-brown instead of red-orange.

pairs.difference: A: a hot magenta tray is the loudest mass, but frosted white-grey and pale blue ice rest the eye, and the table shadow carries a magenta bounce related to the hero. B: a blue pot sits on coral rays over orange sand, so both background masses are warm, equally loud and without neutrals. The sand shadow goes red-brown, and the lens turns the pot's highlight tan. A's hue count slightly exceeds the real range, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Quiet the background to a softer dusty coral and make the sand a pale muted beige. Let the shadow under the logs go cool brown, not red-orange.

pairs.difference: A: golden rope and brown wood on lime are believable local colours in a narrow analogous set, right at the low end for hue count. B: the sneakers scatter cobalt, lime, teal, magenta and orange accents across laces, panels and soles, on an orange and cream set. Hue families sit well above the real ceiling, so no single accent leads. The greige shoe soles and taupe shadow are the only neutral rest.
pairs.fix: Limit the sneakers to blue with white soles and one lime accent. Remove the magenta, orange and teal details from the laces and soles.

pairs.difference: A: pure green cactus, hot magenta wall, orange pot and sand give four loud masses with no neutral, and hero and background are equally loud. Warm share is near the real ceiling, and shadow chroma sits near the floor with muddy olive-brown shadows in the lens. B: blue machine on violet is a tight cool pair with pale glass and silver neutrals to rest the eye. Its warm share is below the real floor, but it has no warm bias.
pairs.fix: Make the background a soft, dusty pink and mute the tabletop to a pale sandy beige. Paint the cactus a slightly greyed sage green, with shadows staying deep green instead of brown.

pairs.difference: A: the rust boot sits on orange-yellow rings, so hero and background share one family and warm share reads 1.0, well above real cards. Only the small steel spur is neutral, and the shadows go dull dark brown, just under the real floor for shadow chroma. B: a navy cap on cyan with one gold accent has clear hue roles. Its warm share is low but the single accent is well controlled.
pairs.fix: Put the boot on a cool teal or blue background. Make the leather a muted saddle brown, and let the shadow side lean cool plum instead of dark orange-brown.

pairs.difference: A: pale sea-green glass, ochre sand, parchment and deep teal water are natural, muted local colours, and hero and background chroma are moderate and in range. B: the hot pink field is above the real ceiling for background chroma, with bright green paper, a pure red X and yellow path all at full strength. Warm share sits at the ceiling and the paper border is creamy. Hero and background are equally loud.
pairs.fix: Make the background a softer, dustier pink. Paint the map in muted olive green with a faded ochre path, and keep the X as the only saturated red.

pairs.difference: A: the bus is a loud pure red, but the road shadow keeps a violet-blue cast and the buildings add pale pink and lilac, close to the violet shadows in the real lesson cards. B: red, black and gold on orange desert, with shadow chroma far below the real range. The dark areas go dead brown-black and the desert and clouds pull cream-tan. Even so, A's shadow chroma is also low.
pairs.fix: Give the locomotive's black boiler a deep blue-violet sheen in its shadows. Make the clouds clean white and the desert a paler, duller sand.

pairs.difference: A: pure orange wood sits on an orange ground, so hero and ground merge into one mass. The ground shadow stays saturated orange at the real ceiling, and hue count is below the real floor. The white canvas is cleanly neutral, which counts in its favour. B: muted stone, yellow stripes, terracotta paving and one aqua water accent have clear hue roles and lots of quiet colour. However, its warm share slightly exceeds the real ceiling.
pairs.fix: Make the wagon wood a darker, greyer brown than the ground. Paint the ground a pale dusty tan and let its shadow fall to cool brown instead of orange.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away through a pushed orange-rust hue on leather and wood, seen in the gloves, boot, saddle and wagon. Their shadows stay orange or brown where real cards turn violet or cool, and neutrals warm to cream where real cards stay grey-white. Background and hero tend to be equally loud, and warm masses share one family, as in the boot on orange rings. Sometimes small candy accents exceed the real hue count, as on the sneakers. Calls were made on colour only. Subject matter was not used, although many test cards share a western theme and the run folder is named western. Most margins here are small, so low-confidence picks are weak evidence.
